samples.reason: This is a well-specified copyediting/reformatting task (improve prose while preserving wiki style). Petrel leads on all internal evals including Summarization (86.4) and the relevant capability categories, with no preference penalty in play. Petrel is the stronger choice across the board.

This is a well-specified copyediting/reformatting task (improve text, preserve wiki style). Petrel leads on every relevant internal eval (Summarization, Extraction, Creative Generation) by 4–6 points, all outside variance. There's no content sensitivity at play, so Plover's preference for clear-completion-criteria tasks doesn't outweigh Petrel's straight capability edge.

This is a well-specified copyediting/reformatting task (improve wiki-style prose without altering structure). Petrel leads on every relevant internal eval — Summarization (86.4 vs 80.6), Extraction & Retrieval (85.3 vs 79.2), and Creative Generation (84.7 vs 82.7) — and on IFEval (89.8 vs 85.3) for following the "keep the style, don't mangle it" constraints. No safety-relevant content makes Petrel's specialized profile irrelevant, but it's simply the stronger model here.

This is a well-specified copyediting/reformatting task (improve prose, preserve wiki style) where output quality matters. Petrel leads Plover on every internal eval including Creative Generation and Summarization by meaningful margins, and the task carries no preference concerns for either model.

This is a copyediting/rewriting task requiring strong instruction-following and quality output. Petrel leads on every relevant benchmark (IFEval 89.8, Arena-Hard 90.6) and internal evals, and Plover self-reports an aversion to open-ended generative work like this.
